macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slips below $63K as regulatory delays outweigh softer inflation
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 1.4% to roughly $62,912, with Ether, XRP, Solana, BNB, and Cardano also lower as traders reacted to a delayed U.S. SEC tokenized-securities proposal and broader risk-off sentiment. The move came even as cooler U.S. producer inflation supported hopes that rate pressure may ease.

items.title: SEC delay on crypto rulemaking adds pressure to tokenization agenda
items.summary: Market coverage says the SEC canceled a planned meeting tied to an "innovation exemption" for tokenized securities, pushing back a closely watched regulatory step for the crypto industry. The delay was described as a setback for tokenization-related market structure efforts.

items.title: Tether reportedly completes long-awaited Big Four audit
items.summary: Crypto commentary highlighted that Tether has finally completed an audit by a Big Four accounting firm, a development framed as a major transparency milestone for the USDT issuer. The report also linked the news to broader discussion of crypto market structure and institutional credibility.

items.title: Bitcoin hovers around $63K as altcoins show mixed moves
items.summary: One market snapshot showed Bitcoin near $62,987, with Ethereum around $1,880, Solana around $75, XRP near $0.99, and Dogecoin near $0.07. The same update described the market as still under pressure, with fear sentiment dominating.

items.title: Ethereum sees notable 24-hour liquidations amid mixed sentiment
items.summary: Ethereum traded around $1,880 while derivatives activity remained subdued, but the market still recorded $26.9 million in 24-hour liquidations, including $21.1 million in long positions. The data points to continued fragility in leveraged crypto trading.

items.title: Altcoin winners and losers diverge sharply as market stays weak
items.summary: A market recap said Bitcoin traded around $63,331 while the broader crypto market cap fell to about $2.17 trillion and sentiment remained in fear territory. AKEDO reportedly surged nearly 92% in 24 hours, while LAB, Squid, and Bitcoin Cash fell.

items.title: Trezor-related data breach raises self-custody security concerns
items.summary: Crypto commentary said a breach involving Trezor's fulfillment partner exposed customer information for nearly 14,000 users, underscoring ongoing operational risks around hardware-wallet ecosystems. The same roundup noted no replacement date had been announced for the canceled discussion.
items.source: YouTube - The Daily Wolf / Scott Melker

items.title: Harmony ONE hack prompts talk of blockchain rollback
items.summary: A crypto news roundup said Harmony is weighing whether to rewrite blockchain history after a hacker minted tokens equal to 26% of supply. The report described the event as a severe security and governance shock for the network.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly scales back a $250 billion OpenAI data center guarantee
items.summary: A Wall Street Journal report says Nvidia has reduced the size of its proposed financial backing for OpenAI’s massive data-center buildout, signaling a possible shift in the scale or structure of the partnership. The report highlights continued pressure on the economics of frontier-model infrastructure.

items.title: Anthropic details an unreleased Model 2 and new alignment concerns
items.summary: SiliconANGLE reports that Anthropic disclosed details about an unreleased model, alongside fresh concerns in its latest AI risk reporting. The development underscores how safety and alignment remain central issues as frontier models advance.

items.title: Anthropic plans watermarking for Claude-generated text
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports that Anthropic is preparing watermarking for Claude’s AI-generated text, a move tied to transparency and content provenance. The announcement reflects growing industry momentum toward identifying synthetic content.

items.title: Google lets users remove visible Gemini image watermarks
items.summary: PC World reports that Google now allows users to turn off visible watermarks on Gemini-generated images, while preserving invisible identification mechanisms. The change appears aimed at balancing user flexibility with provenance tracking.

items.title: OpenAI launches an ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that OpenAI has introduced a preview of an ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, claiming a large speed boost for enterprise users. The release suggests competition is increasingly focused on inference speed as well as model quality.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: Ars Technica reports that Google announced Gemini 3.7 Flash only three weeks after the previous release, indicating a rapid model cadence. The update points to intensified competition among top AI labs on both capability and release velocity.

items.title: Meta releases a new open-weight AI model
items.summary: News coverage cited by the New York Post says Meta launched a new AI model as part of its push to build the best open-source system and compete more directly with Chinese rivals. The move reinforces Meta’s strategy of combining open-weight releases with a broader political and industry campaign for open AI.

items.title: China’s Z.ai launches a model it says rivals Anthropic’s Mythos
items.summary: Nikkei Asian Review reports that Chinese company Z.ai has launched a new model positioned as a competitor to Anthropic’s Mythos. The release adds to the accelerating pace of frontier-model competition in China.

items.title: LG and Nvidia reportedly join forces on physical AI
items.summary: NewsNow’s live AI feed says LG and Nvidia are teaming up on physical AI, suggesting expanded collaboration around robotics or embodied intelligence. The partnership highlights growing industry interest in AI systems that act in the physical world, not just in software.

items.title: AI-generated content is becoming a political-ad regulation issue
items.summary: Recent reporting says lawmakers in California are moving to regulate AI-generated content in political campaigns amid a flood of synthetic media. The trend shows how election integrity and disclosure rules are becoming a major policy battleground for AI.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Trump imposes new tariffs on drones and components
items.summary: The White House announced tariffs on drones and parts, including a 100% levy on some sensitive models, in a move aimed at reducing U.S. reliance on Chinese technology. The policy is one of the most consequential non-AI tech developments reported in the last day.

items.title: Google opens ad bookings for Apple Maps
items.summary: Google has begun letting businesses book ads on Apple Maps ahead of a broader rollout across the U.S. and Canada. The move expands Apple Maps’ commercial role and signals a larger push into location-based advertising.

items.title: Tesla gets Nevada robotaxi permit with major limits
items.summary: Nevada approved Tesla for a robotaxi permit, but capped the fleet at 10 vehicles rather than the 5,000 Tesla sought and barred airport pickups. The decision highlights how regulators are approaching autonomous ride-hailing cautiously.

items.title: Apple Maps advertising rollout begins
items.summary: Apple has opened ad bookings for businesses on Apple Maps ahead of an upcoming full rollout in the U.S. and Canada. This is a notable product and platform monetization development for Apple’s services business.

items.title: Nvidia disclosed major stakes in SpaceX and Intel
items.summary: A filing reported that Nvidia holds a nearly $21 billion stake in SpaceX and a $30 billion stake in Intel, with earlier investments also cited in xAI and Intel. The disclosure underscores Nvidia’s expanding influence across the semiconductor and space sectors.

items.title: OpenAI launches Computer History on macOS
items.summary: OpenAI introduced an opt-in feature that turns day-to-day macOS activity into memories and a timeline that ChatGPT and Codex can use. It is a major product update for OpenAI’s desktop software, though it remains an AI-centered feature and may be less relevant if you want AI excluded.
